findings.title: Keep Kimi's top-level endpoint and credential keys in the private home
findings.body: `KIMI_KEYS` carries only `default_model`, `default_effort` and `default_thinking`, while the existing `kimi_review.sh` preserves top-level `api_key`, `base_url`, `model`, `provider`, `protocol` and size limits. For a supported config such as `default_model = "kimi-k2"`, `base_url = "https://gateway/..."` and `api_key = "..."` (the bare-model form `test_cli_review_wrappers.sh` accepts), the private `config.toml` is written without the endpoint or key, so `kimi -m kimi-k2` talks to the wrong endpoint or fails auth and the attempt falls through or ends inconclusive.

findings.title: Preserve Kimi's dotted provider/model assignments
findings.body: `filter_toml` treats only bracketed lines as tables, so valid TOML dotted assignments such as `providers."managed:kimi-code" = {...}` and `models."kimi-code/k3" = { provider = "managed:kimi-code", model = "k3" }` are ordinary top-level keys and are dropped because they are not in `KIMI_KEYS`; the existing `kimi-dotted-model` fixture says this form must survive. Consequently `kimi_family` cannot read the selected model/provider, so an alias like `default_model = "review"` is skipped as unknown, or when the alias text contains "kimi" the launch runs `-m kimi-code/k3` with no model/provider definition and Kimi fails.

findings.title: Accept a clean Kimi answer after a preamble block
findings.body:
`unbullet` removes bullets but keeps non-verdict blocks, while `parse_answer` accepts a clean answer only when the whole trimmed text is exactly `No findings.`. A Kimi text answer with an earlier read block, e.g. `• Let me read the diff first.

• No findings.` (the same multi-block shape the suite covers for findings), becomes `Let me read the diff first.

No findings.`, is classified `unparseable_answer`, and a clean Kimi review is discarded in favor of another model or an inconclusive result.
